page: Google Cloud Platform a2-ultragpu-2g is an accelerator-optimized virtual machine tailored for intensive machine learning and high-performance computing workloads. The system combines two NVIDIA Ampere A100 GPUs with 80 GB of High Bandwidth Memory each, providing a total of 160 GB of GPU VRAM. The host compute environment consists of 24 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs powered by Intel Xeon processors running at 2.2 GHz across 12 physical cores, accompanied by 38 MB of L3 cache. Memory allocation is substantial, offering 340 GB of system RAM, which yields approximately 14.17 GB per vCPU. Fast scratch storage is bundled via 804 GB of local NVMe SSD space.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong acceleration in large language model inference. The dual-A100 configuration reaches top-tier classification in prompt processing throughput across small, medium, and large models, processing 3091.0 tokens per second on 7B models and 500.14 tokens per second on 70B architectures. Generation speed for 70B models achieves 24.17 tokens per second, also placing in the top ten percent of tested instances. In contrast, CPU-centric benchmarks highlight an architectural emphasis on hardware acceleration rather than scalar processor execution. Single-core stress-ng tests (1201.05) and Geekbench single-core scores (1039.0) sit in the lower quartile, while multi-core metrics, memory bandwidth, and Redis SET throughput remain near median levels.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance consolidates dual high-VRAM accelerators, substantial host memory, and integrated NVMe storage onto a single node, minimizing inter-node networking overhead for medium-scale training and inference. The primary tradeoff is the moderate single-thread host CPU speed, which makes the platform less practical for CPU-bound compiling or decompression tasks. The a2-ultragpu-2g is best suited for large language model serving, deep learning fine-tuning, complex computer vision pipelines, and high-memory scientific simulations requiring dense GPU acceleration.

It features 2 NVIDIA A100 GPUs with 80 GB VRAM each for a combined 160 GB GPU memory pool, backed by 24 dedicated Intel Xeon x86_64 vCPUs running at 2.2 GHz across 12 physical cores. Host memory totals 340 GB, providing an expansive ratio of 14.17 GB per vCPU, while local temporary throughput is supported by 804 GB of integrated NVMe SSD storage. Benchmark results place this instance in the top tier for LLM inference, reaching 500.14 tokens per second in prompt processing and 24.17 tokens per second during generation on 70B parameter models. Host CPU single-thread performance is relatively weak, reflecting its orientation toward GPU acceleration rather than scalar host computing. The a2-ultragpu-2g is best suited for large language model inference, distributed deep learning model training, and memory-intensive scientific simulation.
